story_candidates.title: Thursday at Web Summit: a practical guide to the last day
story_candidates.angle: A practical guide for attendees, and for anyone following from afar, to the last summit day after Wednesday's cancellation: what Web Summit says has changed (stage talks 09:00 to 17:30 through lunch; Wednesday's talks moved to Thursday, with more than 100 of those speakers; 65 community and partner meetups moved, over 125 in total; the app and online schedule to show the new times by Thursday morning), plus Lisbon's weather, how to get there, whether the storm alert has ended, and which side events are on, each checked at its own source.
story_candidates.note: For journalist (summit desk). Ready; time-sensitive: write tonight (20:40), the reviewer checks and publishes from 21:25. Category 'Web Summit 2026' (send the category line with the draft as before). Conditions: (a) The Web Summit facts are Web Summit's, as Vicky read them on websummit.com in her own browser at 20:15 UTC on 11 Nov: attribute each to Web Summit, do not quote Web Summit or its email at length, never read websummit.com by machine, link to Web Summit's schedule page (https://websummit.com/schedule/) instead of copying the schedule, and tell readers the app and online schedule are the place to check times. (b) Check at their own sources, each with its read time: IPMA's outlook for Lisbon on Thursday (IPMA's own data or pages); transport from the operators' own pages or posts (Metro de Lisboa, Carris, CP and others as relevant), saying what each says and when you read it; the end of the alert from the government's or ANEPC's own pages; side events on Thursday using lisbontechfringe.com only as a pointer, each checked at its organiser's own page, and never Luma, Meetup or Eventbrite by machine (an event whose only page is on one of those is left out unless a person has read it). Say what you could not confirm. Link S41, S51, S44 and S54; do not repeat the storm story or the refunds. No contact details, no names of attendees or hosts, no unsupported inference stated as fact; confirmed facts and unknowns apart.
